recipes.name: Healthier Apple Crisp
ingredients_raw: 10 cups unpeeled, cored, and sliced apples

steps.text: Preheat the oven to 350 degrees F (175 degree C).
Place sliced apples in a 9x13-inch pan. Mix white sugar, 1 tablespoon flour, and ground cinnamon together; sprinkle over apples. Pour water evenly over all.
Combine oats, 1 cup flour, brown sugar, baking powder, baking soda, walnuts and melted butter together. Crumble evenly over the apple mixture.
Bake in the preheated oven until golden and crisp on top, about 45 minutes.

raw_recipe.headline: Healthier Apple Crisp
raw_recipe.description: A classic apple crisp is made healthier by using unpeeled apples, less sugar, whole wheat instead of white flour, and adding crunchy walnuts.

review.reviewBody: Oh wow! Best apple crisp ever! I made it as written first time and it was good, but the second time, it was even better when I made these changes: I omitted the white sugar and subbed in brown sugar, doubled the cinnamon, added some ginger (a healthy dash) and some nutmeg (a regular dash). I also omitted the water, it was not necessary and my second batch without the water was a much, much better consistency. (The apples are juicy and release that juice when baked, so go ahead and skip adding that water.) Oh, and in both batches, I used old-fashioned oats, not the quick cooking kind and I subbed corn starch for the flour in the filling, something I always do for fruit pies, cobblers, etc... :-)

I never review recipes but I couldn't let this one go without. I had a crazy amount of apples from my nanas trees and was apple buttered right to death so I decided to switch it up for this apple crisp. I made a pan for both my mother and mother in law (who is an amazing cook) and my mother in law lost her mind when she tasted it. Its all she could talk about all day. I used brown sugar instead of white and doubled the cinnamon. Hands down best apple crisp ever!

Smells delicious, like apple pie! Made 2 pans for healthy potlucks @ husband's & my work. Used 10 large honeycrisp apples, 5. lbs, from local farmer, for each 9 x 13 recipe. It will fill the pan (with a rounded top like a cake), so press the topping on with a large spoon and put the pan on a foil-lined cookie sheet. Followed others' suggestions & added some of my own. Use apple corer/peeler, all brown sugar, all whole wheat fllour, old fashioned oats, 2 tsp. cinnamon, 1 tsp. cloves, & 1/2 tsp. nutmeg. Stir 2 tsp. vanilla extract into melted butter. Wondered whether initial sugar/flour/water mixture would blend in better if it were stirred into apples rather than sprinkled on top. Next time (and there definitely will be a next time!) I would either omit water or add cornstarch or tapioca to water, since it was rather watery. Apples did not get mushy. Tasted great & husband's co-workers ate the entire pan! We were very busy & only had time for 1/2 a pan! It's a keeper!



Revised 10/20/15: Moved to WI & picked fresh apples from our two trees in backyard. Made six 8 x 8 apple crisps already using half a recipe with the following changes: Omit water & sugar (my apples are like red delicious, juicy & sweet), use cornstarch instead of flour in filling, decrease cinnamon to 1/2 tsp, 1/4 tsp. cloves, 1/8 tsp. nutmeg. but keep melted butter @ 1 stick for each topping. (Seems crisper if you mix in 1/2 stick, then pour other half over topping after it cooks 30 min.) Cook 45 min. total.

A keeper, we'll make again. 

We used 4 varieties of apples, sweet to tart, red & green, skin on. Opted for big chunks rather than uniform slices.

Smaller casserole dish, filled to the top with apples, used recommended amount of topping. Based on comments: we mixed apples with flour/spice mix prior to putting in casserole, skipped water, cut sugar to 1/4 cup, replaced white with brown sugar. Doubled cinnamon, added powdered ginger and fresh grated nutmeg (not measured, but at least 1.5 tsp)Added vanilla (might add some bourbon next time) to flour/spice mix, and to butter/oat mix. 

Whole wheat pastry flour, and brown sugar instead of white. Melted butter, but plan to try mixes of butter/olive oil and/or coconut oil in the future. 

Instead of ice cream or whipped topping, we opted for low fat, plain yogurt drizzled on top, may add a trace of honey, molasses or maple syrup next time .. not necessary, but could be a nice addition.

This was so easy and turned out great! I only had 6 apples, so I cut it in half-ish, but went 2/3 on the topping part. I had Macintoshes, which are a bit sweeter, and these particular ones were not very firm. So, I did 1/3 c of sugar, instead of half. Used a stoneware pie dish, and the 45 minutes was perfect. Highly recommend!

I have been making this recipe for years. It is so delicious and satisfying on a cold winter day! I usually half the recipe, which fits perfectly in an 8 x 8 baking dish. 4-5 apples does the trick. Remember to half the measurements in the directions too, though! I also double the cinnamon, add dash of nutmeg, and sub brown sugar for the white sugar and add about a tablespoon more since brown sugar is less sweet than white. 
The most important thing I want to note is that the water is VERY important in this recipe! The first couple times I did not add water, and let me tell you, the juices of the apples are not enough. The recipe calls for the flour, water, and sugar to form a DELICIOUS caramel sauce while baking. Do not leave out the water! I've been adding slightly less than the recipe calls for and it has taken my apple crisp from four stars to five stars! All my taste testers agree!!

It was a hit with everyone! All gone before I thought to take a picture. I used a 3# bag of Golden Delicious and a heaping 1/2 c. of chopped walnuts. I also placed all the slices in a bag, added the sugar mixture to the bag and massaged the apples to give them a nice even coating before putting the slices in the pan. 45 min. in the oven was perfect.

I added a fourth of a cup of ground flaxseed in place of 1/4 cup of the flour. I used whole oats in place of quick oats for more texture. Hubs doesn't like cinnamon so I grated fresh ginger into the apple mixture which imparted a satisfying flavor. This recipe has a great ratio/balance of ingredients.

Good recipe! Per other reviews, used brown sugar exclusively, doubled the cinnamon and added only half the water. Used a food processor for the crumb mixture using cold butter. No melting required! Made this with added craisins and with fresh cranberries for something different. Keeper!
Cut the recipe in half(except for the cinnamon) and baked in 9x9 pan. Came out perfectly!! Will definitely make again very soon.

Really nice, but on the whole I guess I just prefer the unhealthier version. I don't like apple peels in baked goods and the nuts in the topping got a little overcooked for my liking (almost a burnt flavor). I did appreciate the reduced sugar, though. The sweetness was perfect for me. As per another reviewer's suggestion, I omitted the water and found the consistency great.
This was truly delicious! It’s got just the right amount of sweetness. I will definitely be making this again and again! I used pecans instead of walnuts, a personal preference. YUM!
I thought it was perfect!

I made the recipe exactly as is for 1/2 serving, The recipe called for one cup of flour in step 3 part but the ingredient list said a half a cup so I used a half a cup. My recipe turned out very flavorful, however the topping is very crunchy so I'm not sure what I did wrong🥴🫤

Dynamite! I wondered if I could find a better, tried and true crisp recipe that would be a little healthier than those I’ve collected. I used Granny Smith apples and added some organic pumpkin seeds to the chopped walnuts. This will be the new standard dessert in my collection.
I doubled the cinnamon and added a dash of freshly grated nutmeg, used only brown sugar, and added 1 tsp of vanilla extract to the crumble. Thanks for the recipe!

I made the same mistake the other reviewer did- didn't add water because of one of the reviews. When I pulled it out of the oven, the mixture still looked uncooked. I added some water to it and put it back in the oven for 20 more minutes and cranked it up to 375F. It didn't really help but the dish is still tasty regardless of what it looked like. The fact that I am at a higher altitude probably contributed to how it came out.
I skipped the white sugar and it was pretty good. I might use the white sugar in the future. I top it with canned whipped cream and it is very tasty.

The review that was posted as the most helpful said the water wasn't needed so I didn't add it but that was a mistake since it never really came together and when I pulled it out of the oven, the flour/oatmeal mixture was still uncooked. I added some water to it and put it back in the oven for 5 more minutes. It didn't really help but the dish is still tasty regardless of what it looked like. I used Honey Crisp apples and they stayed semi-firm in the crisp.
Easy to make,and delicious!!!
